notes: Target is an M5Stack Core2 with a physically stacked Module13.2 RCA M125.
Module13.2 PAL-M CVBS uses GPIO26, and RCA PCM5102 uses I2S1 BCK GPIO19, DATA GPIO2, LRCK GPIO0.

onboardPeripherals.label: Built-in 2.0 inch 320x240 ILI9342C display
onboardPeripherals.notes: Include <M5Unified.h>, call M5.begin(), and use M5.Display. Reset, backlight, and panel power are controlled through the onboard AXP192.

onboardPeripherals.label: Built-in FT6336U capacitive touch panel
onboardPeripherals.notes: Read through M5.Touch after M5.begin(); do not reinitialize its bus.

onboardPeripherals.label: Built-in NS4168 I2S speaker amplifier
onboardPeripherals.notes: Use M5.Speaker; its I2S pins are unavailable for external wiring.

onboardPeripherals.label: Built-in SPM1423 PDM microphone
onboardPeripherals.notes: Use M5.Mic; GPIO0 is shared with the speaker LRCK signal.

onboardPeripherals.label: Built-in MPU6886 6-axis IMU
onboardPeripherals.notes: Use M5.Imu; it shares the internal I2C bus.

onboardPeripherals.label: Built-in microSD slot
onboardPeripherals.notes: Shares SPI data and clock with the display and uses GPIO4 as CS.

onboardPeripherals.label: Built-in BM8563 real-time clock
onboardPeripherals.notes: Use M5.Rtc; it shares the internal I2C bus.

onboardPeripherals.label: Built-in AXP192 battery and power management
onboardPeripherals.notes: Use M5.Power for battery and power control. The display backlight, reset, and power rails are also managed through this chip.

integratedPower.label: Alimentado pela porta USB do Core2
integratedPower.description: A alimentação chega pela porta USB-C do próprio Core2; não há fonte externa adicionada ao projeto.

tips: Set the M125 physical video selector switch to GPIO26 before powering the stack.
assemblyInstructions.title: Stack the RCA module
warnings: Do not force the connector or stack it while USB power is connected — bent pins or a shifted connector can damage the boards.
assemblyInstructions.description: Turn the Core2 off, line up the Module13.2 RCA M125 underneath it, and press the two units together evenly so the M5-Bus connector is fully seated. This stacked connection carries the PAL-M video and external sound signals.

tips: The firmware creates missing M5RETRO folders. Configure Wi-Fi and API through CONFIGURACOES > CONFIGURAR REDE; the portal writes secrets.json and settings.json. Offline video playback requires neither Wi-Fi nor these files.
assemblyInstructions.title: Prepare the SD card
warnings: Do not put your Wi-Fi password or API token in the firmware; keep them only in secrets.json on the SD card.
assemblyInstructions.description: Format a microSD card as FAT32. Convert media with tools/prepare_video.py and copy each program folder under M5RETRO/videos/. For HTTPS radar, put the server CA certificate at M5RETRO/config/ca.pem.

tips: Select the TV input usually labelled AV, Composite, or Video.
assemblyInstructions.title: Connect the television
warnings: Make sure the yellow video plug is not connected to an audio socket — otherwise the picture will not appear correctly.
assemblyInstructions.description: Plug a composite-video cable from the yellow RCA socket into the TV composite-video input. Plug the white and red RCA sockets into the TV left and right audio inputs.

tips: Use the serial monitor at 115200 baud to view playback statistics. The firmware has been compiled; physical PAL-M/audio validation still requires the device.
assemblyInstructions.title: Power and deploy
warnings: If there is no picture, first confirm the M125 switch is on GPIO26 and the television is set to its composite input.
assemblyInstructions.description: Insert the prepared microSD card and connect the Core2 by USB. Build and upload with PlatformIO as documented in README.md. For Schematik, first run tools/sync_schematik.py and reimport the updated project before deploying.

powerPlan.rationale: O Core2 é alimentado diretamente pela própria porta USB durante o uso e a gravação do firmware.
